tasks.title: A bar chart from a dictionary
tasks.explainer: Real programmers draw charts with **matplotlib**. Your loop builds two lists from the dictionary, then `plt.bar` draws one bar for each planet. Finish the loop so it adds every size, then press Run.

codeStages.label: Starter
codeStages.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

planets = {"Mercury": 4879, "Venus": 12104, "Earth": 12742, "Mars": 6779}

names = []
sizes = []
for name, size in planets.items():
    names.append(name)
    # add the size to the sizes list here

plt.bar(names, sizes, color="orange")
plt.title("How wide are the planets?")
plt.xlabel("Planet")
plt.ylabel("Width (km)")
plt.show()

codeStages.label: Complete
codeStages.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

planets = {"Mercury": 4879, "Venus": 12104, "Earth": 12742, "Mars": 6779}

names = []
sizes = []
for name, size in planets.items():
    names.append(name)
    sizes.append(size)

plt.bar(names, sizes, color="orange")
plt.title("How wide are the planets?")
plt.xlabel("Planet")
plt.ylabel("Width (km)")
plt.show()

tasks.title: A line chart of the week
tasks.explainer: `plt.plot` joins the points with a line. Make the line go through every day's temperature, and give the chart a title.

codeStages.label: Starter
codeStages.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

days = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri"]
temps = [12, 15, 11, 17, 19]

plt.plot(days, temps, marker="o", color="crimson")
plt.ylabel("Temperature (°C)")
plt.show()

codeStages.label: Complete
codeStages.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

days = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri"]
temps = [12, 15, 11, 17, 19]

plt.plot(days, temps, marker="o", color="crimson")
plt.title("Our week of weather")
plt.ylabel("Temperature (°C)")
plt.show()
